references.text: The same command is repeated later in the chapter when God threatens to destroy the congregation because of their rebellion.
Moses conveys God's command to the congregation to stay away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.
Lot is asked to leave Sodom before God destroys the city, a similar pattern where the righteous must be separated from the wicked before judgment.
The prophet Isaiah urges the people to go out and separate themselves from what is unclean, the same theme of separation.
Jeremiah urges the people to flee from Babylon so as not to be struck by God's punishment.
John hears a voice from heaven calling God's people to come out of Babylon so that they do not share in her sins and plagues.
Paul quotes the OT and urges believers to go out from among the unbelievers and separate themselves from them.
God threatens to destroy the people of Israel after the sin of the golden calf, a similar threat of immediate judgment.
God threatens to strike the people with plague and wipe them out after the report of the spies, the same pattern of threatened judgment.
